pack: Amendment Voting Quorum and Veto in postfiatd

rules.claim: Amendment voting is evaluated around flag ledgers: FLAG_LEDGER_INTERVAL is 256, isFlagLedger() is seq % 256 == 0, isVotingLedger() is (seq + 1) % 256 == 0.
rules.title: Flag ledger every 256 ledgers

rules.claim: Amendment doVoting runs only when the previous ledger is a flag ledger and the number of trusted validations is at least validators().quorum().
rules.title: Voting only at flag ledgers with quorum of validations

rules.claim: calculateQuorum returns max(ceil(effectiveUnlSize * 0.67), ceil(unlSize * 0.6)). The comment states the original XRPL uses 80% but this fork uses 67% for devnet/testnet and mainnet should revert to 80%. A command-line minimum quorum overrides; quorum is disabled (SIZE_MAX) when too many publishers are unavailable.
rules.title: Validator quorum is 67% in this fork (floor 60%)

rules.claim: Before fixAmendmentMajorityCalc, threshold = max(1, trusted * 204 / 256) by integer division and an amendment passes when votes >= threshold.
rules.title: Pre-fix majority threshold 204/256 with >= comparison

rules.claim: After fixAmendmentMajorityCalc, threshold = max(1, trusted * 67 / 100) and an amendment passes only when votes > threshold; a single trusted validator is the exception and still uses >=.
rules.title: Post-fix majority threshold 67/100 with strict > comparison

rules.claim: computeThreshold uses integer (truncating) division and max(1, ...), so the effective required share varies with UNL size and is never below 1 vote.
rules.title: Threshold is integer arithmetic with a floor of 1

rules.claim: xrpl.org states an amendment passes when it receives more than 80% support for two weeks. This is the documented rule the code is checked against; it matches neither the pre-fix (79.6875%, >=) nor the post-fix (67%, >) code rule exactly.

external.quote: If an amendment receives more than 80% support for two weeks, the amendment passes and the change applies permanently to all subsequent ledger versions.

rules.title: Docs: more than 80% support for two weeks

rules.claim: The majority-calculation fix is registered as an amendment with Supported::yes and VoteBehavior::DefaultYes, so which threshold regime applies depends on whether that amendment is enabled in the ledger rules.
rules.title: fixAmendmentMajorityCalc is itself a DefaultYes amendment

rules.claim: The simulator computes, for UNL sizes 5, 10, 21, 35 and 100, the smallest number of no-voters that blocks a majority under the pre-fix and post-fix rules. These are model outputs, not source observations.
rules.title: Minimum blocking minority per regime and UNL size

rules.claim: recordVotes ignores validations from untrusted signers; getVotes counts only the cached records of trusted validators that have a live (unexpired) timeout.
rules.title: Only trusted validators' votes count

rules.claim: Each trusted validation's sfAmendments array lists the amendments that validator votes for; a validation without the field clears that validator's cached up-votes.
rules.title: Votes travel in the validation sfAmendments field

rules.claim: TrustedVotes keeps the last vote seen from each trusted validator and expires it 24 hours after the last vote seen; an expired record is cleared to 'no'. The comment says there is no best timeout and the point is to avoid flapping.
rules.title: Trusted votes cached with a 24-hour expiry

rules.claim: trustChanged preserves previously saved voting state for still-trusted validators, gives new validators an empty vote set with an unseated timeout, and destroys the votes of no-longer-trusted validators.

source.anchor: New validators have a starting position of no on everything

rules.title: New trusted validators start with no votes; removed ones lose theirs

rules.claim: doVoting is fed the trusted validations for the previous ledger (parent hash, seq - 1) via getTrustedForLedger, and AmendmentSet is built from the cached TrustedVotes, not from the raw validation set directly.
rules.title: Votes tallied from trusted validations for the previous ledger

rules.claim: Amendment votes are attached to our own validation only when the next ledger is a voting ledger (isVotingLedger), via doValidation on the enabled amendments of the last closed ledger.
rules.title: Our votes are announced only on voting ledgers

rules.claim: The vote list in our validation contains only amendments we support, vote up, and that are not already enabled; the list is sorted before announcement.
rules.title: doValidation announces only supported, up-voted, not-yet-enabled amendments

rules.claim: passes() returns votes >= threshold when trustedValidations_ == 1 even under the post-fix rule, because otherwise a majority would be impossible with one validator.
rules.title: Single trusted validator uses >= even after the fix

rules.claim: veto() returns false unless the current vote is up, then sets down and persists it; unVeto() returns false unless the current vote is down, then sets up and persists it.
rules.title: veto() only flips up to down; unVeto() only down to up

rules.claim: doValidation filters on vote == AmendmentVote::up, so a down-voted (vetoed) amendment is silently absent from our validation's amendment list.
rules.title: A vetoed amendment is never announced in our validations

rules.claim: Votes are persisted with persistVote into wallet.db; [amendments] and [veto_amendments] config sections are ignored with a warning when the FeatureVotes table already exists.

source.anchor: in favor of data in db/wallet.db

rules.title: Vetoes persist in wallet.db and beat the config file

rules.claim: When reading votes from wallet.db, an obsolete amendment's vote is never overwritten; Feature.cpp maps Obsolete to Retired support.
rules.title: Obsolete amendments' votes can never change

rules.claim: When validators say no and the ledger says majority, doVoting emits tfLostMajority; Change::applyAmendment then removes the amendment from sfMajorities, so the two-week hold must start over from a fresh tfGotMajority.
rules.title: Losing majority clears the majority record and restarts the clock

rules.claim: The enable branch of doVoting requires the local vote to be up; a node that vetoes an amendment will not emit the no-flag EnableAmendment pseudo-transaction, though other nodes may.
rules.title: A vetoing node never proposes the enable transaction

rules.claim: A down-vote recorded for an amendment the node has no code for is treated as already vetoed; the node will not vote for an amendment it does not support.
rules.title: Unknown amendments are effectively vetoed already

rules.claim: An amendment listed in both [amendments] and [veto_amendments] logs a warning and is not vetoed by the config parse (the [amendments] entry wins the conflict check).
rules.title: Conflicting config entries warn and the veto loses

rules.claim: The simulator computes, per UNL size and regime, the smallest no-vote coalition that blocks a majority and the delay caused by a one-round dip below threshold. These are model outputs.
rules.title: Minority sizes that block or delay under each regime

rules.claim: xrpl.org states amendments whose source code was removed without being enabled are considered Vetoed by the network. The code expresses the same idea locally (unknown amendments are effectively vetoed) but has no network-wide veto primitive.

external.quote: Amendments that have had their source code removed without being enabled are considered Vetoed by the network.

rules.title: Docs: amendments with removed source are vetoed by the network

rules.claim: defaultAmendmentMajorityTime is 2 weeks (std::chrono::weeks{2}); Config AMENDMENT_MAJORITY_TIME defaults to it and can be configured.
rules.title: Majority must be held for two weeks by default

rules.claim: doVoting emits the enable action only when hasLedgerMajority and (majorityTime + majorityTime_) <= closeTime and the local vote is up.
rules.title: Enable requires majorityTime held up to the close time

rules.claim: Change::applyAmendment records a new majority with close time equal to view().parentCloseTime(), i.e. the close time of the ledger the pseudo-transaction executes in.
rules.title: Majority timestamp is the ledger parent close time

rules.claim: The AmendmentTable.h doVoting adapter builds a ttAMENDMENT pseudo-transaction for the next ledger sequence (lastClosedLedger seq + 1) with the action flags, and adds it to the initial consensus position.
rules.title: Enable pseudo-transaction is injected at flag ledger + 1

rules.claim: needValidatedLedger returns true only when (ledgerSeq - 1) / 256 differs from (lastUpdateSeq_ - 1) / 256, so amendment state is re-evaluated once per flag-ledger interval.
rules.title: Validated-ledger processing only crosses 256-ledger boundaries

rules.claim: xrpl.org states flag ledgers are typically about 15 minutes apart and enabled amendments apply to transactions from flag ledger + 2 onwards. The 15-minute figure is a documentation estimate, not a code constant.

external.quote: The process to enable it happens within the XRP Ledger network, which checks the status of amendments every flag ledger (typically about 15 minutes apart).

rules.title: Docs: flag ledgers about 15 minutes apart; enabled amendments apply from flag + 2

rules.claim: doValidatedLedger tracks firstUnsupportedExpected_ as the earliest majority time among unsupported amendments, plus majorityTime_, so operators learn when an unsupported amendment would activate.
rules.title: First unsupported expected time is earliest majority plus majorityTime

rules.claim: How long two weeks of majority actually takes in wall-clock time on a live network depends on real ledger close cadence and flag-ledger spacing, which cannot be established from the static source tree.
rules.title: Wall-clock duration of the two-week hold on a live network

rules.claim: An EnableAmendment pseudo-transaction with no flags adds the amendment to the ledger's sfAmendments list and calls enable() on the local table.
rules.title: No-flag pseudo-transaction enables the amendment

rules.claim: Change::applyAmendment returns temINVALID_FLAG when a pseudo-transaction carries both tfGotMajority and tfLostMajority.
rules.title: Both majority flags together are invalid

rules.claim: A tfGotMajority for an already-recorded majority, a pseudo-transaction for an already-enabled amendment, and a tfLostMajority with no recorded majority all return tefALREADY.
rules.title: Duplicate majority or enable is rejected as already-applied

rules.claim: When tfLostMajority applies, the amendment's entry is dropped from the sfMajorities array (other majorities pass through unchanged); an empty array makes the field absent.
rules.title: Majority record removed on lost majority

rules.claim: Once an amendment is enabled it can never be disabled; it can only be superseded by a subsequent amendment.
rules.title: Enablement is a one-way switch

rules.claim: If an enabled amendment is not supported locally, Change::applyAmendment calls setAmendmentBlocked(), which sets amendmentBlocked_ and drops the operating mode to CONNECTED; the server can no longer validate, submit, or process transactions.
rules.title: Enabling an unsupported amendment blocks the server

rules.claim: LedgerMaster checks hasUnsupportedEnabled() on each validated ledger and blocks the server; otherwise it re-checks the first-unsupported-expected warning on every flag ledger until the operator upgrades, the amendment loses majority, or it goes live.
rules.title: Unsupported-enabled state is re-checked on validated ledgers

rules.claim: getDesired() returns all known, non-vetoed amendments as the set to enable in the genesis ledger.
rules.title: Genesis ledger enables all known non-vetoed amendments

rules.claim: Feature registration requires that an amendment be supported to be up-voted; the code comment directs DefaultYes only for critical-bug fixes with off-chain consensus, and DefaultNo for new features.

source.anchor: Must be supported to be up-voted

rules.title: Default votes: bug fixes DefaultYes, features DefaultNo

rules.claim: xrpl.org states that when an amendment loses 80% support on the same ledger it reaches the two-week period, EnableAmendment pseudo-transactions are added for both scenarios but the amendment is ultimately enabled. The code emits at most one action per node per round and checks the lost-majority branch before the enable branch, so a node that sees the drop emits LostMajority only; whether the amendment enables depends on which pseudo-transactions from different nodes the consensus set includes. This doc claim is recorded as SPECIFIED and the divergence is modelled in scenario S-11.

external.quote: It's possible for an amendment to lose 80% support on the same ledger it reaches the required two-week period to be enabled. In these cases, an EnableAmendment pseudo-transactions is added for both scenarios, but the amendment is ultimately enabled.

rules.title: Docs: amendment ultimately enabled when support is lost at the deadline
